head.citation-title: Fenton-like catalytic cementitious coating with CoMnFe-LDH@recycled concrete powder for water treatment: In-situ degradation of oxytetracycline and enhanced carbonation curing
head.abstracts: © 2025 Elsevier LtdThis study addresses the urgent need for innovative solutions to mitigate pollution in stormwater runoff by developing the Fenton-like catalytic cementitious coating (FCC) for concrete drainage structure surfaces. The FCC was fabricated by ordinary Portland cement and CoMnFe-LDH/recycled concrete powder (CoMnFe-LDH@RCP) catalyst via carbonation curing. The carbonation curing provided a densified surface with mild pH for CoMnFe-LDH@RCP immobilization and oxytetracycline (OTC) degradation where the OTC removal of 90.72 % in 60 min was achieved by FCC activating peroxymonosulfate. Meanwhile, the incorporation of CoMnFe-LDH@RCP increased the mode pore size and capillary water content of the coating during the pre-curing stage, which enhanced CO2 diffusion and dissolution, and accelerated the carbonation process. This resulted in improved adhesion strength (6.37 MPa) and microhardness (178.73 HV) of FCC. Additionally, the microstructure of CoMnFe-LDH@RCP and FCC was thoroughly characterized and the OTC degradation efficiency, catalytic durability, and physical properties of FCC were evaluated. The impact of CoMnFe-LDH@RCP on the carbonation curing of FCC was discussed by 1H Low-field NMR.

coredata.dc:description: This study addresses the urgent need for innovative solutions to mitigate pollution in stormwater runoff by developing the Fenton-like catalytic cementitious coating (FCC) for concrete drainage structure surfaces. The FCC was fabricated by ordinary Portland cement and CoMnFe-LDH/recycled concrete powder (CoMnFe-LDH@RCP) catalyst via carbonation curing. The carbonation curing provided a densified surface with mild pH for CoMnFe-LDH@RCP immobilization and oxytetracycline (OTC) degradation where the OTC removal of 90.72 % in 60 min was achieved by FCC activating peroxymonosulfate. Meanwhile, the incorporation of CoMnFe-LDH@RCP increased the mode pore size and capillary water content of the coating during the pre-curing stage, which enhanced CO2 diffusion and dissolution, and accelerated the carbonation process. This resulted in improved adhesion strength (6.37 MPa) and microhardness (178.73 HV) of FCC. Additionally, the microstructure of CoMnFe-LDH@RCP and FCC was thoroughly characterized and the OTC degradation efficiency, catalytic durability, and physical properties of FCC were evaluated. The impact of CoMnFe-LDH@RCP on the carbonation curing of FCC was discussed by 1H Low-field NMR.
coredata.dc:title: Fenton-like catalytic cementitious coating with CoMnFe-LDH@recycled concrete powder for water treatment: In-situ degradation of oxytetracycline and enhanced carbonation curing
